q: How many kWh per tonne does a shrimp processing plant use, and how does it compare with the FAO figure?
title: Shrimp plant kWh per tonne: Odisha vs FAO
short: About 1,520 kWh per tonne on average in Bhubaneswar, TERI found: from 1,100 in a large plant in season to 2,850 in a small one off-season. With diesel, that is about 154 kg of oil equivalent a tonne, against the international 83 kgoe from FAO's 2015 figures that TERI cites.
audience: Plant managers and engineers in seafood processing units benchmarking their power use

sections.h: Why the same plant swings so much
p: January to early April is off-season, with output as low as 25% of the yearly average; July to September runs near 160%. Cold stores, chillers and ice machines keep running either way, so kWh per tonne almost triples in a slow month. Average utilisation is only 40 to 60%.

ul: 600 t a year: 9,50,000 kWh and 20 kL of diesel, about 1,583 kWh a tonne.
1,800 t a year: 27,50,000 kWh and 55 kL, about 1,528 kWh a tonne.
9,000 t a year: 1,30,00,000 kWh and 200 kL, about 1,444 kWh a tonne.
DG sets are under 10% of energy.
Repair frosted pipe runs and insulation: 5 to 8% of power, payback under a year.
Automatic refrigeration controls and fan drives: about Rs 1.0 to 1.2 million, payback 1.5 to 2 years.
Drives on condenser fans: 20% less speed cuts fan power about half; payback under a year.
A desuperheater on the ammonia line recovers 12 to 15% of condenser heat as 70 degree water, for about Rs 1.5 to 2.5 million.

sections.h: How to benchmark your own plant
ol: Monthly kWh from your bills, plus DG diesel.
Tonnes packed in the same month.
Compare each month with the same month last year, not with the yearly average.

example.title: From kWh to CO2 per tonne (estimate)
lines: Large plant in season: 1,100 kWh x 0.675 kg = 743 kg CO2
Cluster average: 1,520 kWh x 0.675 kg = 1,026 kg CO2
Small plant off-season: 2,850 kWh x 0.675 kg = 1,924 kg CO2
Gap to the international figure: 154 / 83 = 1.9 times the energy per tonne
example.note: kWh per tonne and the 83 kgoe comparison from TERI's Bhubaneswar profile (2015-16). Grid factor CEA FY 2025-26; DG diesel not included in these lines.

senseible: Senseible turns monthly bills and diesel invoices into the kWh and CO2 per tonne behind your supplier evidence, so a buyer sees your own figure rather than a regional default.

sources.label: TERI, Cluster profile: Bhubaneswar seafood processing industries (2015-16 data)
CEA, CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector (grid factor 0.675 kg CO2 per kWh, FY 2025-26)
